reasons: The cited clause fails the fallback on every material term: it is one-sided (binds only Customer), covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term rather than personnel involved in the Services, bars 'engage' (an effective no-hire, expressly walk-away), runs eighteen months from termination, and has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Deviation classification is correct — this is not an acceptable fallback clause.

The redline lands squarely on the fallback: mutual, twelve months measured from the end of the person's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and an express disclaimer of any no-hire obligation. Deterministic duration and carve-out checks pass.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (ratio 0.849) is not disqualifying here: every material term of the original had to change, so a clause-level rewrite is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position; no extraneous obligations were introduced.

The comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise and in first person plural, states what changed and why, and the cross-reference to § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer made no no-hire commitment) is supported by the quoted text.

Only observation: the preferred position is no non-solicit on Customer at all, and deletion was available; settling at the fallback is a reasonable, well-explained negotiation choice and does not undermine the finding.
